title: Enhancing Financial Inclusion and Regulatory Challenges: A Critical Analysis of Digital Banks and Alternative Lenders Through Digital Platforms, Machine Learning, and Large Language Models Integration

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation and literature review of how credit scoring algorithms might inadvertently produce discriminatory results based on gender due to skewed historical data and proxy variables.

Qualitative evaluation and literature review of how machine learning models in finance can indirectly associate variables like geographical factors with race, leading to discriminatory financial outcomes.
Qualitative evaluation of the regulatory and ethical risks that algorithmic systems in digital banking inadvertently associate financial risk with a user's religion.

Qualitative analysis of how machine learning models trained on past loan data may penalize historically disadvantaged or underrepresented demographics, reinforcing existing inequalities such as unfair credit denials or higher interest rates.
